caption_en:
Every family has roles. Here is Israel's. 🍽️

👵 Grandma: Israeli women live to 85.7 on average (Israel CBS, 2023 data, published 2026).
👩 Mom: 2.9 children per woman, the highest in the OECD, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, where the average is about 1.5 (OECD Society at a Glance 2024; CBS: 2.88 in 2025).
🧒 The kids: one in three Israelis (31.7%) is under 18 (CBS, end of 2024).
👨 Dad: opinions. 5 Knesset elections between April 2019 and November 2022.
🧒 And the young ones: Israel's under 25s rank 3rd happiest in the world (World Happiness Report 2026, via JNS).
🍽️ The whole table: 8th happiest country on Earth (World Happiness Report 2026).

Loud, crowded, nobody agrees. Everybody shows up.

Which seat is yours at this table? Tell me in the comments.

Photos (Wikimedia Commons): Crzrussian (CC BY-SA 3.0); MathKnight and Zachi Evenor (CC BY-SA 4.0); IPPA (CC BY 4.0); Dan Harrelson (CC BY 2.0); Yong Woo Park (CC BY 4.0). AI voice.
caption_he:
עשרה מיליון איש. ארוחת שישי אחת.
סבתא: נשים בישראל חיות בממוצע עד 85.9. אמא: 2.9 ילדים לאישה, הכי הרבה ב־OECD. הילדים: אחד מכל שלושה ישראלים הוא ילד. אבא: דעות. 5 בחירות בפחות מארבע שנים.
והצעירים? השלישיים הכי מאושרים בעולם. והמשפחה כולה: מקום שמיני בעולם באושר.
אף אחד לא מסכים. כולם מגיעים. איזה כיסא שלכם?

sources.label: World Happiness Report, under 25s, via JNS

lines.line: Ten million people. One family dinner.
Every family has roles. Grandma, Mom, Dad, the kids. So let's seat Israel at the table.
Grandma first. She's not going anywhere. Israeli women live to almost eighty six.
Mom. Almost three kids per woman, the most of any developed country. The average? One and a half.
So the kids are everywhere. One in three Israelis is a child.
Dad has opinions. Everyone does. Five elections in under four years.
And the kids? Somehow, the third happiest young people on Earth.
Loud, crowded, everyone talks at once, nobody agrees. And still, the eighth happiest family on Earth.
Which seat is yours at this table?
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
Ten million people. And one family dinner.
